paper_title: Dual Iron-Catalyzed Selective Aerobic Lactonization of 1,6-Diols

questions.question: In the manuscript, what compound does the label '1a' refer to?
questions.ground_truth_answer: 1a is 1,6-hexanediol (the linear diol HO–(CH2)6–OH used as the model substrate).

questions.question: What is compound 2a as presented in the paper (name/structure)?
questions.ground_truth_answer: 2a is ε-caprolactone (the six-membered lactone product derived from 1,6-hexanediol; structure shown in the Schemes).

questions.question: What solvent and reaction temperature were used for the optimized aerobic oxidative lactonization of 1a to give 2a?

Which gave the higher NMR yield of ε-caprolactone 2a: the reaction using BiCl3 as cocatalyst (the early condition reported, Table 1 entry 2) or the optimized Fe(NO3)3·9H2O/TEMPO/FeCl3 conditions (Table 1, entry 16)?
questions.ground_truth_answer: The optimized Fe(NO3)3·9H2O/TEMPO/FeCl3 conditions gave the higher yield (≈70% under the optimized conditions vs 53% with BiCl3).

questions.question: What was the isolated yield (mass and percent) of ε-caprolactone 2a obtained from a 20 mmol scale reaction of 1a under the optimized conditions?
questions.ground_truth_answer: On 20 mmol scale the reaction afforded 1.44 g of 2a corresponding to a 63% isolated yield.
